subject: Computer Networking
title: Mobile Apps vs. Mobile Web
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Mobile Apps vs. Mobile Web.

hook.text: You can use Facebook in a browser or an app. The app feels faster. Why do native apps outperform mobile web?

buildup.text: Native apps store code and assets locally. They only fetch new data from the server, not the entire interface.

discovery.text: Mobile web loads everything fresh each time. On slow connections, that difference in data transfer is noticeable.

twist.text: Progressive Web Apps blur the line. They cache assets like native apps but run in the browser. No app store needed.

climax.text: Both approaches compete. Native wins on performance and features. PWAs win on reach and simplicity.

punchline.text: The best mobile experience depends on the connection, not just the code.

quiz.question: Why do native mobile apps often feel faster than mobile websites?
options: They store code locally and only fetch new data from the server
They use a different internet protocol than browsers
They always have priority on the cellular network

details.summary: Native mobile apps are installed from app stores with full device API access, while mobile web apps run in browsers with progressive enhancement. PWAs bridge the gap with offline support and home screen installation. The choice impacts performance, distribution, development cost, and platform reach.
details.whyItMatters: The native vs web debate affects every mobile product decision. Understanding the trade-offs helps developers choose the right approach for their users and resources.
takeaways: Native apps access device APIs fully but require per-platform code
Mobile web apps reach all devices through the browser instantly
PWAs combine web distribution with app-like offline capabilities

faq.question: When should you build a native app vs a web app?
faq.answer: Build native when you need full device access — camera, sensors, push notifications, or high-performance graphics. Build web when broad reach, instant updates, and low development cost matter more. PWAs are a strong middle ground for content-focused apps.

faq.question: What are the advantages of PWAs?
faq.answer: PWAs install from the browser without app store approval or fees. They update instantly on every visit. They work offline using service workers. They occupy less storage than native apps. However, PWAs have limited access to some device APIs and Apple restricts certain PWA capabilities on iOS.
